neighbours.label: demonstrated possibility: 'possible', 'can', 'could' when something has shown what is achievable ('proves that X is possible', 'an example of what a team can do', 'showed that effort could …'); permission 'can' and 'it is possible that' stay quiet
fire: The clean-up of the harbour proves that lasting change is possible when neighbours work together.
The festival is a fine example of what a few determined volunteers can achieve in a single summer.
Her victory showed that a candidate without money could still win a seat in parliament.
The experiment demonstrates that cheap solar power is possible even in cloudy northern countries.
The rebuilt bridge is proof of what a small village can do when everyone lends a hand.
His recovery showed the other patients that patience and effort could bring real results.
The school's success shows that excellent teaching is possible in the poorest parts of the city.
The record flight was a reminder of how far a light aircraft can travel on a single tank.
quiet: The clean-up of the harbour began in May, when the neighbours agreed to work together.
Volunteers at the festival can leave their bags in the tent beside the main stage.
It is possible that the candidate will lose her seat in parliament next month.
It is possible that the solar panels will arrive late because of the cloudy weather.
Visitors to the village can cross the rebuilt bridge on foot or by bicycle.
The other patients could hear the television from the room at the end of the corridor.
It is possible that the school will move to another part of the city next year.
Passengers on the light aircraft can bring a single small bag on the flight.
